text.p: The following are the main stories from Wednesday morning's Austrian newspapers:
DER STANDARD
- Organisation for Security and Cooperation in Europe names former chancellor Franz Vranitzky as special envoy to Albania.
- Hofburg theater director Claus Peymann blames Austria's political climate for his decision not to seek reappointment when his current term expires in 1999.
- Audit office criticises Bank Austria for not having realised sufficient synergies from the takeover of GiroCredit two years ago.
- Fibremaker Lenzing reports a group pre-tax loss of 160 million schillings, says had to make 500 million schillings loss provisions for its U.S. subisidiary.
- Research institute IHS says inequality among Austria's population is on the rise.
- A planned cooperation between steelmaker VA Stahl and Germany's steel trading company Kloeckner was called off after the companies failed to resolve their differences.
- Austria's oil an chemicals group OMV plans to expand its network of petrol stations in Croatia and the Czech Republic. Expansion plans in Poland have been put on hold.
DIE PRESSE
- Audit office criticises Bank Austria for extending a 250 million schilling credit to newspaper Der Standard two years ago even though the paper's economic future appeared in doubt.
- Almost 40 percent of Austrians say the introduction of Europe's single currency will be disadvantageous to them, a new study shows.
- Austria's telecoms and transport ministry calls for bids for the country's third mobile phone network, expects to award the license by the end of July.
KURIER
- Tightened border controls, implemented after a number of immigrants was caught trying to cross the border illegally, are causing long delays at Austria's borders.
- Economic research body IHS says the state-run pension system will collapse by the year 2030 unless it is reformed immediately.
- Austria's unemployment rate remained steady at 4.1 percent in February, employment rose slightly.

- EU commission to publish its decision on the sale of state's controlling stake in Creditanstalt to its main rival Bank Austria next week. Bank Austria to raise three billion schillings in fresh capital in June.
- Austria Tabak, reporting record earnings of 1.8 billion schillings for 1996, expected to be privatised via the stock exchange this year.
KRONEN ZEITUNG
- Approval ratings of Austria's coalition government of Social Democrats and conservative People's Party rise as unemployment falls.
